html:
Musqueam land is the homeland of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm, a Coast Salish people at the mouth of the Fraser River, where the city of Vancouver now stands. Their language is hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓, a form of Halkomelem.

People have lived at the river mouth for thousands of years. The Musqueam village site of c̓əsnaʔəm, also called the Marpole Midden, holds the remains of a village thousands of years old. The Fraser's huge salmon runs fed large villages of cedar plank houses.

The city of Vancouver grew over their land from the 1880s, and the Musqueam were left with small reserves. In 1990 a fishing case brought by a Musqueam man, R. v. Sparrow, led the Supreme Court of Canada to rule that Aboriginal fishing rights are protected by the constitution. The Musqueam were one of four host First Nations of the 2010 Winter Olympics. Neighbours: Tsawwassen, Tsleil-Waututh and Squamish.
